programme: FOSL1 (AP-1/FRA-1) drives an ECM-remodeling and inflammatory-cytokine programme (MMP1, MMP2, MMP9, MMP13, CXCL8, IL6, CCL2, PLAUR, FN1, ELN, NOS3); TCF7 drives a Wnt/T-cell effector programme (IFNG, IL17A, IL2, CD4, VEGFA) that licenses and recruits infiltrating lymphocytes; GRHL2 maintains the junctional/barrier gene set (CDH1, CLDN3, CLDN4) whose loss is a precondition for that infiltration. Together these three describe a vascular/neurovascular-barrier-breakdown axis: junction loss, AP-1-driven matrix remodeling, and T-cell entry.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease this axis corresponds to blood-brain-barrier endothelial dysfunction and perivascular/parenchymal T-cell infiltration, both increasingly recognized components of the vascular contribution to AD pathology rather than a purely neuronal process.
role_in_b: In cardiovascular disease this is the canonical atherosclerotic/vascular-remodeling programme: AP-1-driven MMP induction and ECM turnover in the vessel wall, endothelial junction loss, and T-cell-mediated plaque inflammation.
shared_axis: Both diseases require an endothelial/epithelial barrier (held by GRHL2's junction genes) to fail before AP-1/FOSL1-driven matrix remodeling and Wnt/TCF7-licensed T-cell entry can proceed; atherosclerotic plaque and AD neurovascular/BBB breakdown would then be two tissue-specific readouts of the same breakdown-and-infiltration sequence.
reasoning: The module is nameable from three of the twelve factors and each of FOSL1 and TCF7 is independently placed in Alzheimer's disease by retrieved papers, so this is not built from nothing. But no factor has any Open Targets association or literature placement in Cardiovascular Disease at all, so the CVD half of the claim rests on the general, well-established biology of AP-1/MMP-driven plaque remodeling rather than on anything retrieved here — hence moderate, not strong.
support: 37775708 — places FOSL1 in a shared endothelial-cell metabolic-shift signature between stroke and Alzheimer's disease (the vascular angle used here); 39349220 — mentions FOSL1 in a Bacopa monnieri/interleukin-signaling neuroprotection context in AD, weaker and not specifically vascular; 41794902 — places TCF7 in the T-cell-receptor profile of CD8+ T cells accumulating in AD brain (the infiltration angle used here). None found placing FOSL1, TCF7, or GRHL2 in Cardiovascular Disease.
how_to_falsify: In matched AD and atherosclerotic vessel/BBB endothelial single-cell or spatial data, test whether FOSL1-high/TCF7-high endothelial or perivascular clusters actually co-occur with GRHL2-target junction loss (CDH1/CLDN3/CLDN4 downregulation) and local T-cell infiltration; if FOSL1/TCF7 activity is high without junction loss or infiltrate, or vice versa, the proposed sequence is wrong.
caveats: Blood|brain tissue pairing, 64 patient-group comparisons from only 6 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance count is not 64 independent replications. No Open Targets record exists for any of the 12 listed factors in Cardiovascular Disease. Seven of the twelve concordant factors are HOXA/B/C paralogs with no retrieved literature and no CVD association; they were left out of the carrying set because their target sets (other HOX genes, BMP4/7, FGF8, TEK, EPHA3/4/7, TH) look like a positional/developmental identity signature rather than this remodeling-and-infiltration mechanism, and their high concordance may instead reflect shared anatomical/tissue-of-origin structure across cohorts. SRSF2 (tau-exon-10 splicing) and GTF2I (broad, diffuse growth/cell-cycle targets) are each individually documented but do not integrate into the barrier/remodeling axis and are excluded. The tissue-generic exclusion list already removed lineage-defining blood/endothelial factors (RELB, IRF8, SPIB, ERG, PRDM1, SOX10), so the remaining signal is not simply blood-cell composition, but it is also not large: only 3 of 12 factors carry the story argued here.
